functional.text: The system shall display the operational status (active or inactive) of all ten modules on the main dashboard.
The system shall display cumulative detection statistics: total files analysed, malware detected, benign files and model accuracy.
The system shall provide persistent sidebar navigation to every screen.
The system shall display a feed of the most recent detection events.
The system shall let the user filter the detection history by malware family, minimum confidence and date range, and sort it by time.
The system shall let the user export the filtered detection history as a CSV file.
The system shall show in the sidebar whether a model is loaded, whether the dataset is available and which file is currently uploaded.
The system shall let the user start and stop the Digital Twin IIoT simulation from the dashboard.
The system shall display a live log of the traffic exchanged between simulated IIoT nodes.
The system shall display the status of each simulated node (PLC, HMI, sensor, sandbox).
The system shall display a chart of simulated traffic by protocol (Modbus, MQTT, other).
The system shall execute each sample inside an isolated container network with no route to the host's network.
The system shall capture the network traffic of each simulation run and export it as a Zeek conn.log for dynamic analysis.
The system shall show the planned Digital Twin architecture and live checks of its deployment prerequisites (Docker, Zeek, behaviour model).
The system shall accept PE and ELF binaries of up to 50 MB, identified by their magic bytes (MZ or 0x7F ELF).
The system shall convert an accepted binary into a 128 × 128 grayscale image and display it within 3 seconds.
The system shall display the file's metadata: name, size, format and SHA-256 hash.
The system shall display a 256-bin pixel intensity histogram of the image.
The system shall reject an empty, oversized or non-PE/ELF file with an error message that states what happened, its cause and the action to take.
The system shall lay out the bytes using the Malimg (Nataraj) file-size width table before resizing, so that uploaded binaries match the training images.
The system shall load the Malimg dataset (one folder per family) and validate its integrity, reporting corrupt images, class counts and the imbalance ratio.
The system shall encode family labels as contiguous integer indices and normalise pixel values before training.
The system shall split the dataset into stratified training, validation and test sets (70 / 15 / 15) with a fixed random seed.

The system shall provide optional augmentation of training images with random rotation, flips and brightness changes (disabled by default after the Evaluation 3 ablation showed it lowers accuracy on byte images).
The system shall provide optional Gaussian-noise injection into training images, as part of the augmentation option.
The system shall balance the training data with class-aware oversampling so that every family is drawn with equal probability in each epoch.
The system shall display a dataset gallery with sample images and the number of images per family.
The system shall train the CNN with configurable epochs, learning rate, batch size, oversampling strategy and augmentation on/off, from the dashboard or the command line.
The system shall display training progress and log output while training runs, and allow the user to stop it.
The system shall save the best model weights (by validation accuracy) and the class list, and reload them for inference.
The system shall evaluate the model on the held-out test set and report accuracy, precision, recall, F1, the confusion matrix, ROC-AUC, per-class false positive rate and MCC.
The system shall report results on a class-balanced test set (equal samples per family, repeated random draws) together with balanced accuracy.
The system shall measure detection of families not seen in training with a leave-families-out experiment.
The system shall include a Benign class built from clean system binaries and measure the false positive rate on clean files.
The system shall run the detection model on the uploaded binary when the user requests it.
The system shall display the top-1 family with a confidence bar coloured green (≥ 80%), amber (50–79%) or red (< 50%).
The system shall display a chart of the probability of every class.
The system shall display a Grad-CAM heatmap over the binary image when the user requests it.
The system shall display the MITRE ATT&CK for ICS tactics and techniques of the predicted family.
The system shall generate downloadable PDF and JSON forensic reports.
The system shall explain the Grad-CAM colours in text and let the user download the heatmap overlay as a PNG image.
The system shall present a file classified as Benign as benign, show no MITRE techniques for it and count it under benign files.
The system shall parse Zeek conn.log and IoT-23 conn.log.labeled network captures.
The system shall extract behavioural features from each flow without using IP addresses.
The system shall classify each flow as Benign, PortScan, C&C, DDoS, Attack, FileDownload or Okiru behaviour.
The system shall compute a capture-level score and verdict (MALICIOUS, SUSPICIOUS or BENIGN).
The system shall explain the capture verdict with feature importance and each feature's deviation from benign traffic.
The system shall map observed behaviours to MITRE ATT&CK for ICS techniques.
The system shall provide a Dynamic Analysis screen to upload a capture and view its results.
The system shall fuse the static confidence and the dynamic score into one verdict with an agreement category (confirmed, static only, novel variant, no evidence).
The system shall combine the MITRE techniques of both sources, tagged by the source that supports them.
The system shall provide a Hybrid Verdict screen with a what-if simulator for the fusion rules.
The system shall evaluate fusion on paired static and dynamic evidence of the same samples.
When a binary is uploaded, the system shall validate it, read its bytes and build the 2-D image.
When detection is requested, the system shall load the model, preprocess the image and run a forward pass.
When a detection result is available, the system shall log the event to SQLite without blocking the result.
When a report is requested, the system shall compile it with the MITRE data of the predicted family.
When the Digital Twin is started, the system shall create the containers and the isolated network.
When a heatmap is requested, the system shall compute Grad-CAM through hooks on the last convolutional layer.

nonfunctional.text: Identical input shall give identical results (variance < 0.5% over 10 runs).
Corrupt or malformed files shall be handled without a crash.
The Digital Twin shall run for at least 4 hours between failures.
No detection record shall be lost on an unclean shutdown (SQLite WAL).
Two concurrent dashboard sessions shall not interfere with each other.
A first-time user shall complete upload and detection in under 5 minutes.
Visual indicators shall be interpretable without a machine-learning background.
Every error message shall state what happened, its cause and the action to take.
Technical terms shall have tooltips.
Reports shall download in under 10 seconds and open in standard viewers.
Conversion shall take < 3 s for files ≤ 10 MB and < 10 s for files ≤ 50 MB.
Inference shall take < 5 s on CPU and < 1 s on GPU.
The dashboard shall render within 4 s on the local network.
Grad-CAM shall take < 8 s on CPU and < 3 s on GPU.
Report generation shall take < 10 s.
The database shall hold 100,000 records with queries under 500 ms.
Uploaded files shall be processed only inside an isolated container.
The Digital Twin network shall be isolated from the host network.
The database file shall have permission 600 (owner read/write only).
SHA-256 shall be computed locally, with no external service.
The dashboard shall be bound to localhost by default.

use_cases.name: Upload Binary File
use_cases.desc: The analyst uploads a suspicious PE or ELF binary, which is validated and converted into a grayscale image.
main: Analyst opens the Binary Upload screen.
Analyst selects a file.
System checks the size (≤ 50 MB) and the magic bytes.
System computes the SHA-256 hash and converts the bytes to a 128 × 128 image.
System displays the image and confirms the upload.
alt: 3a. File is empty, larger than 50 MB or not PE/ELF: system shows an error stating what, cause and action; the use case ends.
use_cases.post: The image and metadata are held in the session for detection.

use_cases.name: View File Analysis
use_cases.desc: The analyst inspects the uploaded file's metadata, image and byte histogram.
main: System displays name, size, format and SHA-256.
System displays the grayscale image.
System displays the 256-bin pixel histogram.
alt: 1a. No file uploaded: system asks the analyst to upload one first.

use_cases.name: Run Malware Detection
use_cases.desc: The analyst runs the CNN on the uploaded binary to obtain its malware family and confidence.
main: Analyst opens Malware Detection and clicks Run Detection.
System runs the CNN and computes class probabilities.
System displays the top-1 family with a colour-coded confidence bar and the probability chart.
System logs the detection event to SQLite.
System maps the family to MITRE ATT&CK for ICS (UC-04).
alt: 1a. No file uploaded: system shows guidance to upload one.
2a. No trained model: system explains how to train one; the use case ends.
3a. Predicted class is Benign: system shows the file as benign and no MITRE techniques.
use_cases.post: A detection result exists and is recorded in the detection log.

use_cases.name: Map to MITRE ATT&CK for ICS
use_cases.desc: Included use case: looks up the ICS tactics and techniques of a malware family or an observed behaviour.
use_cases.pre: A family or behaviour label is available.
main: System looks up the label in the local MITRE mapping file.
System returns the tactics and the techniques (ID and name).
alt: 1a. Label not in the mapping: system returns an empty mapping and says so.
use_cases.post: Tactics and techniques are displayed by the including use case.

use_cases.name: View Grad-CAM Explanation
use_cases.desc: The analyst asks which regions of the binary drove the prediction.
main: Analyst enables the Grad-CAM option.
System computes Grad-CAM on the last convolutional layer for the predicted class.
System overlays the heatmap on the image and explains the colours.
Analyst may download the overlay as PNG.
alt: 2a. Grad-CAM fails: system shows an error; the detection result is unaffected.
use_cases.post: The heatmap is available for the report.

use_cases.name: Generate Forensic Report
use_cases.desc: A PDF or JSON forensic report of the detection is produced for download.
main: Actor chooses PDF or JSON report.
System compiles file details, prediction, top-3 classes, MITRE mapping (UC-04) and heatmap if present.
System offers the report for download and records a report event.
alt: 2a. PDF library unavailable or generation fails: system shows an error and still offers JSON.
use_cases.post: A report file is downloaded and a report event is logged.

use_cases.name: Analyse Network Capture
use_cases.desc: The analyst uploads a Zeek conn.log of a sample's traffic to classify its network behaviour.
main: Analyst opens Dynamic Analysis and uploads a conn.log.
System parses the flows and extracts 61 IP-free features.
System classifies every flow and computes the capture score and verdict.
System shows behaviours, the most influential features and MITRE techniques (UC-04).
alt: 1a. File is not a valid conn.log: system shows an error stating what, cause and action.
1b. No behaviour model: system explains how to train one; the use case ends.
use_cases.post: A capture score is available for the hybrid verdict.

use_cases.name: View Hybrid Verdict
use_cases.desc: The analyst sees one verdict that combines static and dynamic evidence, with the reason for it.
use_cases.pre: A static result (UC-03), a capture score (UC-07), or both, exist.
main: Analyst opens Hybrid Verdict.
System fuses the two scores with weights 0.5 / 0.5.
System assigns MALICIOUS, SUSPICIOUS or BENIGN and the agreement category.
System lists the MITRE techniques of both sources, tagged by source.
alt: 2a. Only one source available: verdict is computed from that source alone.
2b. Neither available: system offers the what-if simulator only.
use_cases.post: The hybrid verdict can be downloaded as JSON.

use_cases.name: View Dashboard and Detection History
use_cases.desc: The actor reviews module status, detection statistics and the filterable detection history.
main: Actor opens the main dashboard.
System shows module status and detection statistics.
System lists recent detections.
Actor filters the history by family, confidence and date, and may export it to CSV.
alt: 3a. No detections yet: system says the history is empty.

use_cases.name: Prepare Training Dataset
use_cases.desc: Included use case: loads, validates, splits, augments and balances the Malimg dataset.
use_cases.pre: The Malimg dataset (and optionally the Benign class) is present on disk.
main: System validates dataset integrity and reports class counts.
System encodes labels and makes a stratified 70/15/15 split.
System builds the training loader with augmentation and class-aware oversampling.
alt: 1a. Dataset missing or empty: system reports the expected folder; the use case ends.
use_cases.post: Balanced training, validation and test loaders are ready.

use_cases.name: Train Detection Models
use_cases.desc: The researcher trains the CNN (and, from the command line, the behaviour model).
main: Researcher sets epochs, learning rate, batch size and oversampling strategy, and starts training.
System prepares the dataset (UC-10).
System trains the model and shows progress and log output.
System saves the best weights and class list and reloads the model.
alt: 3a. Researcher stops training: system terminates the job and keeps the last best weights.
3b. Training fails: system shows the error output.
use_cases.post: A trained model is saved and loaded for detection.

use_cases.name: Evaluate Detection Model
use_cases.desc: The model is evaluated on held-out data, a class-balanced test set, unseen families and clean files.
main: Researcher runs the evaluation.
System computes the metrics on the full test split.
System computes the metrics on repeated class-balanced draws.
System saves metrics and plots; the evaluator views them.
alt: 1a. No model: system reports that training must be run first.
use_cases.post: Metrics files and plots are saved.

use_cases.name: Run Digital Twin Simulation
use_cases.desc: A sample is executed inside the isolated IIoT twin and its traffic is captured.
main: Actor starts the simulation with a sample.
System creates the PLC, HMI, sensor and sandbox containers on an internal network.
System runs the sample and records traffic with Zeek.
System stops the twin and exports the conn.log.
alt: 2a. Docker unavailable: system reports the missing prerequisite.
use_cases.post: A conn.log of the sample's behaviour is available for UC-07.

use_cases.name: Monitor Digital Twin
use_cases.desc: While a simulation runs, the researcher watches node status and traffic.
main: System shows each node's status.
System streams the traffic log.
System shows traffic by protocol.
alt: 1a. A node stops: system marks it as down.

use_cases.name: Check Twin Prerequisites
use_cases.desc: The administrator checks whether the machine is ready to host the Digital Twin.
main: Administrator opens the Digital Twin screen.
System checks Docker, Zeek and the behaviour model.
System shows each check as passed or missing with the action to fix it.
